name: Addie at Metro Center
headline: Addie at Metro Center (developed as Atria at Metro Center Station) is a 222-home, four-story apartment building for adults 55 and older at 30% to 70% AMI, across from the Aurora Municipal Center; Dominium's project entity won a 2022 federal 4% award with $51.6M of CHFA bonds.
why_it_matters: It is one of the largest senior tax-credit buildings in metro Denver, uses income averaging (exactly 60% AMI on average) and drew Aurora HOME money and Aurora bond cap, so lease-up at 70% AMI rents is worth watching.

status.label: Construction financed in early 2024; completion and 8609 not confirmed
status.detail: April Housing said in January 2024 that Blackstone was providing $37M of credit equity to start construction. The deal is still on CHFA's 2026-09-21 list, which leaves out developments with 8609s issued. No dated public record of completion or opening was found.

next_step: Watch for a certificate of occupancy or opening announcement and for the deal to move to CHFA's 4% completed-developments (8609) report.

key_numbers.meaning: 106 one-bedroom and 116 two-bedroom apartments, all income-restricted.
About $45.9M over 10 years; no state credit.
Tax-exempt private activity bonds issued by CHFA; Aurora had committed $5M of its own bond cap in 2022.
From Blackstone through April Housing, announced January 2024.

facts.value: In a qualified census tract; not in a DDA
Four-story Type V wood frame, about 289,000 sq ft, 53-space partly underground garage, clubhouse, pool and spa
Clubhouse, business center, fitness room, library, beauty salon, pocket park and public art
Across from the Aurora Municipal Center, near RTD light rail

money.note: Amount marked subject to change by CHFA. Annual credit, runs 10 years.
Recommended by Aurora's review committee in March 2022 for 'Aurora Metro Center Station Senior Housing'; final contract amount not found.

money.source: City of Aurora private activity bond cap
money.note: Approved by City Council on 2022-05-09 as part of a $21M round; staff recommended routing Aurora's $21,387,505 2022 allocation through the Aurora Housing Authority to the three projects.

parties.name: Aurora Leased Housing Development I, LLC
April Housing (Blackstone Real Estate portfolio company)
City of Aurora (with Aurora Housing Authority as conduit for the 2022 bond cap)

background.text: CHFA's name (Addie at Metro Center) differs from the name used in 2024 by April Housing and the engineer (Atria at Metro Center / Atria at Metro Center Station); they are taken to be the same project because of the matching 222 senior units, Dominium sponsorship and location across from the Aurora Municipal Center (inferred).
Aurora's March 2022 funding round noted the project's shovel-readiness and recommended $1M HOME and $5M of private activity bonds for 'Aurora Metro Center Station Senior Housing' (222 senior units).

Aurora City Council approved the first Community Development Investment round on 2022-05-09, including $5M of bond cap for the project; by July 2022 the project was listed among HUD-funded projects needing environmental review.
The income mix averages exactly 60% AMI, consistent with the income-averaging test; 40 units at 70% AMI are offset by 22 units at 30-50% AMI (inferred from CHFA's mix).
It is described as Dominium's first development in Aurora and its third with April Housing and Blackstone.

timeline.event: Aurora housing committee reviews recommendation of $1M HOME and $5M bonds
Aurora City Council approves first Community Development Investment round, including $5M bond cap
April Housing announces $37M of Blackstone credit equity to begin development
Still on CHFA's active 4% award list (no 8609 yet)

discrepancies.text: CHFA's report lists the building as Addie at Metro Center, while April Housing's 2024 release and the structural engineer call it Atria at Metro Center.
April Housing's release headline places the development in Denver, while CHFA and the release body place it in Aurora.
